role: independent reviewer, R2. Not HQ. Does not adjudicate, adopt or self-adopt.
method: Structural field-path walk of the parsed JSON. Every scalar string was visited with its full dotted/indexed field path and every maximal hex run of 8 or more characters was extracted with a non-hex boundary assertion on both sides. NOT a grep: this is deliberately immune to the truncation failure mode.
why_method_matters: A truncated grep would undercount and could misattribute a prose restatement to a field. The walk distinguishes fields from narrative text, which is what resolves the two clarifications below.

failure_mode_check.why: This is the check most exposed to the truncation failure mode, because a census invites grep. I used a structural field-path walk instead, which cannot silently absorb a prose restatement as a field and cannot miss a field because a line was cut. The two discrepancies I found are exactly the discrepancies a grep would have produced, which is evidence the method change was necessary rather than cosmetic.
